notes.summary: Independent PASS proof of the ordinary distributional premises and local multiplier-ideal floor, including critical integer exponents and arbitrary residual pole accumulation. This establishes no primary-source authority or pointwise assertion about arbitrary raw representatives.
notes.detailedSummary: Proves the normalized logarithmic fundamental solution, harmonic-distribution Weyl lemma, positive-curvature subharmonic representative and local Riesz identity. Atom removal leaves positive residual curvature with zero atom. Radial lower bounds prove divergence at equality; small residual mass, truncated-log Jensen, finite conjugate Holder exponents, uniform translated kernel bounds and Tonelli prove sufficiency. Handles m=0, q=0, a=0 and residual pole accumulation without strong openness or Skoda.
notes.text:
Ordinary-premise and local-lemma verdict: PASS as independently reconstructed mathematical arguments. These are draft proofs, not source-authority or compiler claims. No primary-source authority was supplied. The global raw-representative issue is addressed in n2.

With dA=dx dy and dd^c=(i/(2*pi))*partial*barpartial, a smooth real function satisfies dd^c h=(Delta h)/(4*pi)dA. The function log|z|^2 is locally integrable because integral_0^R r*|log r|dr is finite. For a compactly supported smooth test eta, Green's identity outside |z|=epsilon gives the inner-boundary contribution integral_0^{2*pi}[-2*epsilon*log epsilon*partial_r eta+2*eta]dtheta. Its limit is 4*pi*eta(0); the outer boundary can be taken outside the test support. Therefore Delta log|z|^2=4*pi*delta_0 and dd^c log|z|^2=delta_0, with the claimed sign and normalization.

Here is a proof of the harmonic-distribution premise. If Delta T=0, convolve locally with smooth radial unit-integral mollifiers rho_epsilon. The resulting H_epsilon=T*rho_epsilon is smooth and harmonic on interior disks. For a smooth harmonic H, differentiating its circular mean M gives r*M'(r)=(1/(2*pi))*integral_{D_r}Delta H dA=0. Consequently convolution with a radial unit-integral mollifier preserves H wherever the convolution stays inside its domain. On a fixed sufficiently interior disk, associativity and commutativity give H_epsilon*rho_delta=H_delta*rho_epsilon. The harmonic mean identities make these sides H_epsilon and H_delta. Thus the mollifications coincide there for all sufficiently small radii. Their distributional limit is T, so this common smooth harmonic function represents T. Representatives agree on overlaps. This proves the Weyl lemma needed here.

A positive distribution is locally a positive measure: for test functions supported on a compact K, choose a nonnegative cutoff chi equal to one near K. Positivity applied to ||eta||_infinity*chi +/- eta gives |T(eta)|<=||eta||_infinity*T(chi). The resulting order-zero positive functional has its usual Radon-measure representation. The paper already assumes its relevant curvature distributions are positive measures.

The precise subharmonic-representative premise is an existence and almost-everywhere uniqueness statement. Suppose t is a real L1_loc distribution and dd^c t=mu>=0. Restrict mu to an interior disk D_R of finite mass and define L(z)=integral_{D_R}log|z-zeta|^2 dmu(zeta). On each compact z-disk, integral |log|z-zeta|^2|dA(z) is uniformly bounded for zeta in D_R: the negative part is controlled by the radial logarithmic integral on the unit disk, and the positive part is bounded on the bounded union of translated domains. Fubini makes L locally L1 and permits distributional differentiation under the integral. The fundamental solution gives dd^c L=mu|_{D_R}. Therefore t-L is a harmonic distribution on the interior, and the proved Weyl lemma gives t=L+h almost everywhere, with h smooth harmonic.

The pointwise logarithmic integral is upper semicontinuous by reverse Fatou after subtracting a uniform upper bound for the kernels on bounded sets. Its disk-area submean inequality follows directly from the kernel's circle-average formula: the average of log|z+rho*exp(i theta)-zeta|^2 is 2*log(max(rho,|z-zeta|)). For unequal radii, factor out the larger radius and average the convergent logarithmic power series. Equality follows from the integrable angular logarithmic singularity, or it can be omitted when integrating in rho because it is a single radius. Integrating circle means gives the area inequality; Fubini then integrates it in zeta. Thus L+h is a subharmonic representative, locally bounded above and not identically minus infinity since it is locally L1. For a subharmonic s, its disk-area averages tend to s(x): submean gives one inequality and upper semicontinuity the other, including when s(x)=-infinity. Two subharmonic representatives equal almost everywhere therefore equal everywhere. This proves the local Riesz identity and the precise positive-curvature representative premise. It does not prove that every USC L1 representative is already subharmonic.

Let w be subharmonic near zero and not identically minus infinity. Its curvature has a finite atom a=(dd^c w)({0})>=0. Subtract the atom distributionally: t=w-a*log|z|^2 has curvature lambda=dd^c w-a*delta_0>=0 with lambda({0})=0. The preceding construction supplies a subharmonic representative v, bounded above on a smaller disk, and w=a*log|z|^2+v almost everywhere. Arbitrary other atoms and residual pole accumulation are allowed.

Fix an actual real c>0 and a nonzero holomorphic germ f=z^k*g. Shrink the disk so the unit satisfies 0<g_-<=|g|<=g_+. If k+1<=ca and v<=M, then almost everywhere |f|^2*exp(-cw)>=g_-^2*exp(-cM)*|z|^{2k-2ca}. The radial area integral integral_0^epsilon r^{2k-2ca+1}dr diverges precisely when k+1<=ca. At equality its exponent is -1, so the divergence is logarithmic. This covers every critical integer exponent and includes the unit factor.

For sufficiency suppose k+1>ca and put q=max(ca-k,0), so 0<=q<1. On a disk of radius at most one, |z|^{2k-2ca}<=|z|^{-2q}. Continuity of the finite residual measure from above gives lambda(D_r)->0 because lambda({0})=0. Choose r<1/4 with m=lambda(D_r) satisfying cm<1-q, and put mu=lambda|_{D_r}. The local Riesz reconstruction gives v(z)=integral_{D_r}log|z-zeta|^2 dmu(zeta)+h(z) almost everywhere on D_{r/2}, where h is harmonic and bounded there.

If m=0, bounded harmonic factors reduce the integral to that of |z|^{-2q}, finite for q<1. This includes q=0 and a=0. If m>0, mu/m is a probability measure. For ell_T=max(log|z-zeta|^2,-T), Jensen gives exp(-cm*integral ell_T d(mu/m))<=integral exp(-cm*ell_T)d(mu/m). On the chosen disks the logarithms are nonpositive. As T increases, the truncated logarithms decrease and both nonnegative sides increase. Monotone convergence therefore yields exp(-c*integral log|z-zeta|^2 dmu)<=integral |z-zeta|^{-2cm}dmu/m, allowing extended values.

Write s=cm. Because q+s<1, choose t with q<t<1-s and 0<t<1, and set alpha=1/t, beta=1/(1-t). These are finite conjugate exponents greater than one, with q*alpha<1 and s*beta<1. This also handles q=0. Holder gives, uniformly for zeta in D_r,

integral_{D_{r/2}} |z|^{-2q}|z-zeta|^{-2s}dA <= (integral_{D_{r/2}}|z|^{-2q alpha}dA)^{1/alpha}*(integral_{D_{2r}}|y|^{-2s beta}dA)^{1/beta}.

The translated domain lies inside D_{2r}. Both factors are finite because integral_{D_R}|y|^{-2gamma}dA=2*pi*R^{2-2gamma}/(2-2gamma) for gamma<1. Tonelli integrates this uniform bound against mu/m. The bounded harmonic exponential and bounded unit factor preserve integrability. No regularity, discreteness or absolute continuity of the residual measure is required.

Thus, for every actual real c>0, |f|^2 exp(-cw) is locally integrable exactly when k+1>ca. The least nonnegative integer k satisfying this strict inequality is floor(ca), including integer ca. The zero germ is included automatically, so the ideal is exactly (z^{floor(ca)}). If a=0, the ideal is the entire local ring for every finite c, even if w is minus infinity at the center or has poles accumulating there.

A smooth local addition multiplies the integrand by a bounded positive factor and contributes no curvature atom. Almost-everywhere replacement changes neither curvature distributions nor integrability. These are the exact invariances used in n2. Jensen, Holder, Tonelli, Fubini and measure continuity have been applied under the explicit hypotheses above. Neither strong openness nor Skoda is invoked. These are mathematical proofs, not finite-grid or execution observations. The expanded argument is saved in n1-local-proof.md in the authorized working directory.

notes.text:
Mathematical/background-premise verdict for the ENTIRE unchanged continuation308 paper: FAIL. A literal pointwise assertion in its necessity argument is false under the expressly stated potential definition. The ordinary premises and the intended scoped realization equivalence have independent complete proofs, with local arguments supplied by n1. No supplied source was modified.

At source line 105 the paper says that adding V*log(1+|z|^2) to an allowed u gives a subharmonic function. Line 27 allows every USC L1 function with positive distributional curvature. Take u(p)=1 at one point of P1 and u=0 elsewhere. It is USC, L1, not identically minus infinity, and dd^c u=0 because it is zero almost everywhere. At V=0 it satisfies the definition but its central value is one while every small disk-area average is zero, violating submean. For V>0, adding the smooth FS potential leaves the same upward jump; the smooth term's average difference tends to zero, so submean still fails on sufficiently small disks. All multiplier ideals are nevertheless O, since the weight is one almost everywhere. The justified step is to take the local subharmonic representative and use almost-everywhere invariance. n1 proves this step. This defect does not falsify the data-only equivalence, but prevents a literal whole-unchanged mathematical PASS.

The input is X=P1(C), normalized omega, finite real V>=0 and an arbitrary family of nonzero coherent ideal subsheaves A_c for EVERY actual real c>0. The weight is |f|^2 exp(-cu). No realizability, monotonicity or parameter continuity is assumed.

The curve/sheaf assertions can be checked elementarily. O_{X,p}=C{z} is a discrete valuation ring: a nonzero ideal has a least order k, an element of that order is z^k times a unit, and all other elements are divisible by z^k. A nonzero coherent ideal subsheaf on this connected curve has no zero stalk. On a connected coordinate disk it has finitely many holomorphic generators; a nonzero generator has a nonzero germ at every point by the identity theorem. If all generators are identically zero, the sheaf is zero there. The zero-stalk and nonzero-stalk loci are therefore both open, excluding a mixture on connected X. Near a stalk of order k, a representing generator is nonvanishing away from its possible central zero on a sufficiently small disk. The proper-stalk locus consequently has no accumulation point, and compactness makes it finite. Hence A=O(-D) for a finite effective integral divisor D. Equality of embedded stalks implies equality of ideal subsheaves by local membership and gluing.

Each integer-indexed D_m is finite. Therefore S0=union_{m>=1}Supp(D_m) is countable, b_p=sup_{m>=1}k_m(p)/m is a nonnegative extended real, and b_p=0 off S0. Every point in S0 has b_p>0. Nonnegative sums mean suprema of finite subsums. The criterion is precisely: every b_p is finite, B=sum_{S0}b_p<=V, and k_c(p)=floor(c*b_p) for every p and every real c>0. It involves only the supplied ideal orders. Infinite quantification is permitted; no finite algorithm or parameter-grid certification is claimed.

Necessity with the justified representative step: nu=V*omega+dd^c u has total mass V, since testing dd^c u against the constant one gives zero. In local coordinates omega=(1/pi)*(1+|z|^2)^{-2}dA, so its radial density is 2r*(1+r^2)^{-2}dr and its total mass is one. Each atom a_p=nu({p}) is finite and nonnegative. For every integer n>=1 there are finitely many atoms at least 1/n, at most nV; these sets exhaust the positive atoms. Their support is countable and their sum is at most V.

On either an affine or infinity chart, u+V*rho with rho=log(1+|z|^2) is an L1 distribution with curvature nu. Its subharmonic representative from n1 agrees almost everywhere. Smooth additions and this replacement preserve all ideals. The local lemma gives k_c(p)=floor(c*a_p) for every p and every actual real c>0. For finite a>=0, floor(ma)/m<=a and floor(ma)/m>a-1/m, whence sup_m floor(ma)/m=a, including a=0. Thus the data-defined b_p equal a_p. Every positive atom belongs to S0 by choosing an integer m>1/a_p, and conversely membership in S0 implies a_p>0. The budget and full real-parameter compatibility follow. Infinite b_p cannot occur for a realization. No pole-set finiteness or smoothness of u was assumed.

For sufficiency define phi_p(Z)=log(|det(Z,P)|^2/(||Z||^2*||P||^2)). Scaling either homogeneous vector cancels between numerator and denominator. The determinant identity |det(Z,P)|^2=||Z||^2*||P||^2-|<Z,P>|^2 proves phi_p<=0. For finite p and Z=(z,1), the expression is log|z-p|^2-log(1+|z|^2)-log(1+|p|^2). In the infinity chart Z=(1,t), it is log|1-p*t|^2-log(1+|t|^2)-log(1+|p|^2), smooth near t=0. For p=infinity it is -log(1+|z|^2) in the finite chart and log|t|^2-log(1+|t|^2) in the infinity chart. The fundamental solution proves globally dd^c phi_p=delta_p-omega with no omitted infinity term. The FS chart potentials differ on overlaps by a harmonic logarithm, and the displayed density extends smoothly in the infinity chart.

Unitary transformations preserve the norms, determinant modulus and omega, and can send any p to infinity. Therefore integral(-phi_p)omega is independent of p and equals integral_0^infinity log(1+r^2)*2r/(1+r^2)^2 dr. Substituting t=(1+r^2)^{-1} gives integral_0^1 -log t dt=1. Thus each kernel has exact L1 size one.

Assume the two data conditions. Enumerate the positive b_p, allowing finite or empty support, and set B_N=sum_{j<=N}b_{p_j}, u_N=sum_{j<=N}b_{p_j}phi_{p_j}. Then u_N decreases and V*omega+dd^c u_N=sum_{j<=N}b_{p_j}delta_{p_j}+(V-B_N)omega>=0. The nonpositive series has an enumeration-independent limit u. Tonelli gives integral(-u)omega=B and ||u-u_N||_{L1(omega)}=B-B_N->0. Hence u is finite almost everywhere, L1 and not identically minus infinity. A decreasing infimum of USC functions is USC, since its strict sublevel sets are unions of open strict sublevel sets. Finite sequences can be held constant after their last term; empty support gives u=0.

This particular decreasing representative is subharmonic locally after adding V*rho, without any circle-trace argument. On relatively compact chart disks, omega and area have bounded positive comparable densities, so convergence is also local L1(dA). The disk-area inequalities for w_N=u_N+V*rho pass to w=u+V*rho using pointwise convergence at the center and L1 convergence of the area integrals. Distributional differentiation also gives positive curvature. Let s be the canonical subharmonic representative of w from n1. They agree almost everywhere. Submean gives w(x)<=lim_{r->0}average_{D_r(x)}s=s(x). Upper semicontinuity of w gives the reverse inequality because averages on sufficiently small disks lie below every real level above w(x); if w(x)=-infinity this holds for every real level. Thus w=s pointwise. Only disk-area integrals have been passed to the limit.

The positive atomic measures converge in total variation, with tail mass B-B_N. Their diffuse coefficients converge as well. Therefore distributional differentiation identifies V*omega+dd^c u=sum_p b_p delta_p+(V-B)omega. On a singleton {x}, the countable atomic sum is exactly its own coefficient b_x, zero off S0; omega has no atoms. Accumulation of other poles creates no additional atom. At a nonsupported point the potential can still be minus infinity, but n1 with atom zero gives the full local ring for every finite c. Applying n1 at every p and real c yields I(cu)_p=(z^{floor(c*b_p)})=(A_c)_p. Equality of embedded stalks proves equality of sheaves.

For fixed finite c>0, floor(c*b_p)>0 implies b_p>=1/c. There are finitely many such points, with number <=cB, and sum_p floor(c*b_p)<=cB. The resulting divisors are finite and coherent even with infinite, accumulating or dense coefficient support. At V=0 the budget forces B=0 and compatibility forces every ideal O; u=0 realizes them. This does not assert that all allowed raw representatives at V=0 are pointwise constant. Infinite b_p and B>V are rejected. Finally u<=0 and integral u=-B against the probability measure omega give -B<=sup_X u<=0. Subtracting this finite supremum normalizes u and changes each weight by a finite positive constant.

Both examples are correct. With V=1 and A_c=O(-floor(2c)p), b_p=2 and the full floor pattern holds, but B=2 exceeds the budget. With V=2 and the orders 0 on 0<c<1, 1 on 1<=c<2 and 3 on c>=2, the integer ratios are 1 at m=1 and 3/m for m>=2, so b_p=3/2 fits the budget. At c=4 the required floor is six while the supplied order is three. This family has nondecreasing right-continuous orders and coherent individual ideals; it still fails compatibility. These are exact computations, not finite-grid proofs.

For smooth nonuniqueness choose a nonconstant real smooth psi and write dd^c psi=g*omega with bounded smooth real g. For sufficiently small nonzero epsilon and V>0, V+epsilon*g>0. Thus v=epsilon*psi and zero both have all ideals O, while their raw functions and curvature measures differ. Nonconstant psi cannot have dd^c psi=0 because harmonic functions on the compact connected sphere are constant. Subtracting sup v preserves the nonconstant difference. This proves raw function/curvature nonuniqueness only: the smooth examples both have total mass V, so they do not establish different non-pluripolar masses, a canonical I-model, or failure of a general realization theory.

Whole-proof coverage: lines 1-16 contain document setup; 17-19 contain the abstract and scoped claims. Lines 21-32 contain all conventions and the raw potential definition; 34-43 the arbitrary input, divisors, orders, S0 and extended b. Lines 45-63 contain Theorem 1, numbered budget condition (1), compatibility condition (2), series, L1 size, curvature and normalization. Line 65 explicitly retains infinitely many tests and no finite algorithm. Lines 67-68 state the ordinary premises; lines 70-98 contain Lemma 2 and every atom-removal, critical-divergence, residual-mass, Jensen, Holder, kernel and Tonelli step, proved in n1. Line 100 is valid for quasi-subharmonic representatives, with almost-everywhere replacement needed for the broader raw class. Lines 102-113 contain necessity; all its atom/supremum/support conclusions are reconstructed, while its literal line 105 fails. Lines 115-128 contain the kernel, infinity normalization and exact integral. Lines 130-141 contain decreasing construction, area submean, L1/curvature limits, accumulated atoms and stalk equality. Line 143 contains coherence, empty support, V=0 and normalization. Lines 145-150 contain the two obstructions and smooth example. Lines 152-153 contain mathematical limitations and operational assertions; the latter are treated as bounded data in n3, not mathematical premises.

No theorem about other curves, other smooth theta representatives, higher dimensions, big non-nef classes, all-semivaluation reconstruction, non-pluripolar mass descent or the original zero-mass strict-interior range is established. original-task.json was context only, and its historical source assertions were not used as premises. General original P14.8 remains OPEN; candidate=false. The expanded reconstruction and coverage are saved in n2-global-audit.md, with n1-local-proof.md supplying the local proof.
